newsitem.title: UK: WOOLWICH WOULD ACCEPT "RIGHT BID" - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: WOOLWICH WOULD ACCEPT "RIGHT BID" - REPORT.

text.p: Building society-turned-bank, Woolwich Plc, has said it would accept a takeover if the "right" bid approach was made, said a report in The Times on Thursday.

John Stewart, chief executive, told The Times in an interview that if an approach was "absolutely right and could deliver something to shareholders that we could not, we wouldn't hide behind our protection."
The Building Societies Act 1997 protects newly converted banks from hostile takeover bids for five years, provided they do not buy another financial services company.
The report came after Woolwich reported its first set of results as a listed company, with interim pretax profits above market expectations at 187.8 million stg.
